title: Answer sentence extraction (foundational)
description: Signature original: A generated answer is split into individual sentences, each treated as a claim candidate, while boilerplate like greetings and transitions is filtered out. Only sentences that assert something checkable proceed to the audit; opinions and rhetorical questions are marked non-factual and skipped. This keeps the auditor focused on statements that could actually be wrong. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import re
answer = 'Hello! The archive holds 52,268 databases. It is quite impressive, really. Growth continues daily.'
sents = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', answer) if s.strip()]
factual = [s for s in sents if not re.match(r'(?i)^(hello|hi|thanks|it is quite)', s)]
print('sentences:', len(sents), '| factual candidates:', len(factual))
for s in factual: print(' -', s)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Claim-to-Source Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Per-sentence evidence alignment (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each factual sentence is aligned against the retrieved evidence passages using token overlap with entity emphasis, exactly like the evidence chain builder's linker. A sentence passes when at least one passage scores above the support threshold; the best-scoring passage becomes its cited support. Sentences are audited independently so one weak claim does not sink its well-supported neighbors. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
def align(sent, passages):
    s = set(sent.lower().split())
    best = max(passages, key=lambda p: len(s & set(p.lower().split())) / max(1, len(s)))
    sc = len(s & set(best.lower().split())) / max(1, len(s))
    return best, round(sc, 2)
sent = 'the archive holds 52268 databases'
print(align(sent, ['the archive holds 52268 databases today', 'weather is sunny']))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Claim-to-Source Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Unsupported-claim flagging (foundational)
description: Signature original: Sentences with no supporting passage above threshold are flagged as unsupported and returned with their exact text, not paraphrased away. The flag distinguishes 'no evidence retrieved' from 'evidence contradicts', because the remedies differ: the first needs more retrieval, the second needs the answer rewritten. Flags accumulate into the audit verdict for the whole answer. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
audited = [('the archive holds 52268 databases', 0.9), ('it was founded on mars', 0.1)]
TH = 0.35
for sent, sc in audited:
    print(('SUPPORTED ' if sc >= TH else 'UNSUPPORTED ') + sent[:50])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Claim-to-Source Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Citation presence and placement check (foundational)
description: Signature original: The auditor also checks that the answer's citations actually point at the passages used for support, not at decorative references. Each citation marker is resolved to a passage, and the passage is re-scored against the sentence it supposedly supports. Orphan citations and mismatched pairings are reported as formatting faults even when the underlying claim is true. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Claim-to-Source Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Audit report with pass/fail verdict (foundational)
description: Signature original: The audit ends in a structured report: per-sentence support scores, the list of unsupported claims, citation faults, and an overall verdict of pass, pass-with-notes, or fail. Failed answers are routed back for regeneration with the unsupported claims listed as explicit constraints. The report is stored with the answer so readers can see exactly what was checked. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
report = {'sentences': 4, 'supported': 3, 'unsupported': ['it was founded on mars'], 'citation_faults': 0}
report['verdict'] = 'fail' if report['unsupported'] else 'pass'
print('audit verdict:', report['verdict'])
print('needs rewrite:', report['unsupported'])
